beats.title: World
beats.headline: Pope back in square; Israel count; Abiy, Isaias in Moscow.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Pope Leo back in St. Peter’s Square for the audience
stories.body: Pope Leo rode the popemobile through St. Peter’s Square this morning, Rome time, and gave his Wednesday catechesis outdoors. Continuing his series on Gaudium et Spes, he said faith “enriches and brings to fulfillment every culture it encounters” and must itself “become a culture that is shaped by Christ.” Beforehand he met Mercedes-Benz executives marking a century of the Popemobile, urging that technology serve human dignity, creation and the common good.
stories.why: The catechesis series on the Council’s Gaudium et Spes continues weekly ahead of the Nov. 6 trip to South America.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Cardinal Romeo’s funeral this morning; the Pope’s November calendar
stories.body: The funeral of Cardinal Paolo Romeo, Palermo’s archbishop from 2006 to 2015, is at 11 a.m. Rome time, 6 a.m. Eastern, in Acireale’s cathedral. In his condolence telegram, Pope Leo called him a “dear brother who generously served the Gospel,” recalling his years as papal representative in Haiti, Colombia, Canada and Italy. The Vatican also released the Pope’s liturgies ahead: All Souls’ Mass at Rome’s Verano Cemetery on Nov. 2, a Mass for deceased cardinals and bishops on Nov. 5, then the Nov. 6–17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Saint Peter’s Basilica turns 400 on Nov. 18
stories.body: On returning from South America, the Pope will celebrate Mass on Nov. 18 for the fourth centenary of the dedication of Saint Peter’s Basilica, consecrated in 1626. On Dec. 8 he goes to Piazza di Spagna for the traditional act of veneration of Mary Immaculate. The trip itself will include a meeting with survivors of clergy abuse, the Vatican confirmed Tuesday.

stories.headline: Africa: Abiy and Isaias both in Moscow as Russia offers to mediate
stories.body: The third Russia–Africa summit opens today in Moscow with 48 countries taking part, 22 led by heads of state. Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed meets Putin today; Eritrea’s President Isaias Afwerki, who arrived Tuesday, sees him Friday. Russia has offered a venue for Ethiopia–Eritrea contacts, and China says a special envoy will tour the region, but neither neighbor has accepted. On the ground, federal forces captured senior Tigrayan commander Maj. Gen. Yohannes Woldegiyorgis on Oct. 26, while Fano militias in Amhara attack the supply roads into Tigray.
stories.why: Both leaders in one city is the closest the two sides have come to talks since ties broke down; Ethiopia says it will talk only on three conditions.

stories.headline: Africa: Ebola outbreak is now the world’s second largest ever recorded
stories.body: With 10,060 confirmed cases and 4,887 deaths, Congo’s Bundibugyo outbreak is now the second-largest Ebola epidemic on record, and more than 2,700 of the infected are children, Save the Children says. A nurse was killed in an attack on health workers answering an alert. Kenya has nine linked cases, and Nigeria’s single case has been evacuated to Switzerland. The Norwegian Refugee Council is calling for an urgent scale-up of the response, and a treatment trial called TUMAINI began in Bunia on Oct. 23.

stories.headline: Africa: UN warns sieges in Kordofan and Blue Nile could repeat El Fasher
stories.body: Marking a year since El Fasher fell to the Rapid Support Forces, UN officials called for accountability and an immediate ceasefire and urged both the army and the RSF to pull their forces out of cities. The UN’s genocide-prevention adviser warned that sieges in Kordofan and Blue Nile could open the way to new atrocities. Amnesty says fewer than 70,000 people remain in a city that once held more than a million, and 17 of the 19 people it interviewed had been detained.

stories.headline: Asia: Overnight count puts Netanyahu’s bloc at 54, short of a majority
stories.body: With about 71 percent of votes counted by Wednesday morning in Israel, Netanyahu’s bloc has 54 of 120 seats, the Eisenkot-led opposition 47, and Arab-led parties 19. Likud leads with 27 seats, ahead of Eisenkot’s Yashar at about 21, and turnout was 77.7 percent. Eisenkot has left the door open to working with Arab parties under conditions. Soldiers’ ballots are still being counted. President Trump said Netanyahu “did very well” and the race “might be winning or tie.”

stories.headline: Asia: Gulf states draft a peace deal as Houthis claim a refinery strike
stories.body: The Guardian reports Gulf states are building a multipart deal: Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within four days of sanctions being lifted, and the Houthis would withdraw. The U.S. and Europe also want UN inspectors readmitted to Iran. Iran had earlier demanded seven days. Meanwhile the Houthis say they hit Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura refinery, causing a fire, with a ballistic missile, which Riyadh has not confirmed, and the Wall Street Journal reports the U.S. told Gulf allies to prepare for a “short, intense” campaign against Iran after the midterms.

stories.headline: Asia: Cyclone Arnab kills three in Andhra Pradesh after overnight landfall
stories.body: Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast between 2 and 8 a.m. local time Wednesday and weakened to a severe cyclonic storm. Three people died, one under a falling tree in Bhimavaram and two from downed live wires. About 57,000 people are in relief camps in Andhra Pradesh and 30,000 were evacuated in Odisha, with crops on roughly 70,900 hectares damaged.

stories.headline: Europe: Overnight, a missile and 88 drones; fire in Kharkiv injures a child
stories.body: Russia fired an Iskander ballistic missile and 88 attack drones, 38 of them jet-powered, overnight, Ukraine’s Air Force said; 71 drones were downed and eight sites were hit. A large fire broke out in Kharkiv’s Osnovianskyi district, injuring five people, among them a four-year-old. Across Ukraine, Russian attacks killed two people and injured 17 over the past day.

stories.headline: Europe: Oleshky truce passes 30 hours “without a single incident”
stories.body: Ukraine’s human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets says the first 30 hours of the Oleshky ceasefire passed with no incidents. Russia’s rights commissioner Tatyana Lantratova says it runs until 10:59 p.m. Moscow time on Nov. 1. Oleshky, across the Dnipro from Kherson, is under Russian occupation; the truce is meant to let civilians leave and supplies get in once roads are de-mined.

stories.headline: Europe: Trump hopes to meet Putin and Zelenskyy; France braces for protests
stories.body: Back from Texas overnight, President Trump said he hopes to meet Putin and Zelenskyy soon and that “a lot of progress” has been made; Putin has said Russia is ready to resume U.S.-mediated talks next month. In France, a Ligue 1 match in Lyon was moved because of nationwide protests planned for Saturday over living costs and school conditions. Turkey says it will load fuel at its first nuclear plant, Akkuyu, within weeks.

stories.headline: North America: Trump ends Biden’s methane rule at a Lubbock rally
stories.body: At Tuesday night’s rally in Lubbock, Texas, the President announced he is ending the Biden-era methane rule for oil and gas, claiming 45 billion dollars in savings and 210 million more barrels of oil. The rule had been projected to prevent 58 million tons of methane emissions by 2038. Environmental Defense Fund’s Fred Krupp called the repeal a “free pass” for polluters. Supporters say it will lower energy costs as fuel prices stay high during the Iran war.

stories.headline: North America: On the tarmac, Trump welcomes Flávio Bolsonaro and eyes Xi talks
stories.body: Returning to Joint Base Andrews overnight, the President said he would “approve” of Brazil’s defeated candidate Flávio Bolsonaro coming to the U.S., calling Brazil’s election “very strange.” He said a nuclear-disarmament meeting with China’s Xi Jinping is scheduled and that he will attend the ASEAN summit in Manila in November. The midterm elections are Tuesday, Nov. 3.

stories.headline: North America: WSJ: Gulf allies told to expect strikes on Iran after the vote
stories.body: The Wall Street Journal reports the U.S. has told several Gulf countries to prepare for a “short, intense military campaign” against Iran after the Nov. 3 midterms. A Patriot battery is moving from Texas to the region, troops have been pulled from exposed bases, and bombers are being readied.

stories.headline: South America: Flávio Bolsonaro lands in Miami despite a court travel ban
stories.body: Brazil’s defeated presidential candidate arrived in Miami on Tuesday, met by his brother Eduardo, O Globo reports, despite a judicial ban on travel. President Trump said overnight he would approve of the visit. Brazil’s Federal Police have canceled his passports.

stories.headline: South America: Delcy Rodríguez retraces Machado’s route: “Let no one interfere”
stories.body: Venezuela’s acting president toured Aragua and other states along the road María Corina Machado traveled on her return, warning “radical sectors” not to meddle with the country’s “stability.” She promised relief “soon” from worsening blackouts, citing 7,400 megawatts to be added with General Electric and Argentina’s Impsa. She called Machado’s trip a “show.”

stories.headline: South America: U.S. soldiers train in Colombia through Nov. 11
stories.body: More than 300 U.S. troops are at Tolemaida, Colombia’s largest base, for the Vanguardia del Sur exercise on counternarcotics, illegal mining, drones and medical evacuation. Critics in Congress say lawmakers must authorize it; the government says training missions don’t need approval.

stories.headline: Oceania: Australia’s inflation jumps to 4.3 percent, driven by fuel
stories.body: Headline inflation rose to 4.3 percent in September, and Treasurer Jim Chalmers blamed the Middle East war and fuel prices. The Reserve Bank’s chief economist says he sees no recession ahead. The Star casino group was also fined 260 million dollars.

stories.headline: Oceania: Bomb threat at Parliament House as MPs’ safety stays in focus
stories.body: Federal police searched the Senate wing after a bomb threat shortly before lunch and found nothing. Police told a hearing there were nearly 800 threats against MPs in six months, and Senator Fatima Payman apologized to Helen Haines for remarks about the attack that cost the MP both legs.

stories.headline: Oceania: Marles meets Hegseth; Rocket Lab flies from New Zealand
stories.body: Defence Minister Richard Marles met U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at the ASEAN defence ministers’ meeting on the sidelines of the regional talks. From New Zealand, Rocket Lab’s 98th Electron put three HawkEye 360 satellites into orbit.

stories.body: Promise: cut regulations and unleash American energy. Action: the President announced the end of the Biden methane rule for oil and gas wells, in a Lubbock rally speech. Impact: the President claims 45 billion dollars in savings and 210 million more barrels; the rule had been projected to prevent 58 million tons of methane by 2038. Supporters see cheaper energy, and critics like EDF call it a “free pass” for polluters.

stories.headline: Ending the Ukraine war: Oleshky truce, day two
stories.body: Promise: end the war. Action: the First Lady’s local ceasefire in Oleshky passed 30 hours without an incident, and the President says he hopes to meet Putin and Zelenskyy soon. Impact: a real, if small, humanitarian opening; skeptics note a missile and 88 drones hit elsewhere in Ukraine the same night.

stories.headline: Peace through strength: Iran strikes after the midterms?
stories.body: Promise: stop Iran’s nuclear program. Action: per the Wall Street Journal, Gulf allies have been told to expect a “short, intense” campaign after Nov. 3, while Gulf states race to finish a peace deal that would reopen Hormuz. Impact: supporters say pressure is pushing Iran toward terms; critics warn of a wider war and higher fuel prices.

stories.headline: MAHA and recovery: Kennedy in Detroit for the STREETS program
stories.body: Promise: treat homelessness and addiction as problems to heal, not manage. Action: Secretary Kennedy visited Detroit, one of eight STREETS communities, each getting 3 million dollars a year for four years for street-based treatment, recovery and housing; Miami-Dade County is another. Impact: the Michigan Advance notes he promoted faith-based recovery after controversy over earlier remarks about Arab Americans. Results will be measured in people housed and sober, not announcements.

stories.headline: MAHA: the breast cancer screening push, one day on
stories.body: Promise: prevention and early detection. Action: HHS’s new effort spreads proven screening and follow-up practices through more than 40 health systems and adds breast-density education. Impact: hospital groups welcomed it; the number to watch is how quickly women get follow-up after an abnormal mammogram.

stories.headline: Tesla: closed at $407.46, then the Robotaxi fleet passed 1,000 in Texas
stories.body: Tesla rose 4 percent Tuesday to 407.46 dollars and traded near 408 overnight. Benzinga reports 1,051 Robotaxis in Austin, with Cybercabs (544) now outnumbering Model Ys (507). After Governor DeSantis asked for Miami and Tampa service to include the beaches, Musk replied, “Coming soon.” Tesla’s Miami zone is 31 square miles, against Waymo’s 60.

stories.headline: Tesla: hiring in Vietnam; a Semi fire shuts a California freeway
stories.body: Tesla is “officially coming to Vietnam,” a recruiter posted, listing five management jobs weeks after registering a local subsidiary of about 3 million dollars, in a market where VinFast holds about 36 percent of car sales. Less happily, a Tesla Semi fire shut Interstate 880 in Hayward, California. BlackRock’s stake has slipped below 5 percent through dilution.

stories.headline: SpaceX: SPCX up 1.1 percent to $148.58
stories.body: SpaceX shares closed Tuesday at 148.58 dollars, up 1.14 percent. Investors are weighing the 40-billion-dollar AI-chip financing for its AI unit, the former xAI, and Bloomberg’s report that the committees studying a Tesla merger are stacked with Musk allies. Starship Flight 15 is targeted for Nov. 8.

stories.headline: Starlink: next launch Friday morning from California
stories.body: The next Falcon 9 Starlink mission, Group 15-18, is set for early Friday, Oct. 30, from Vandenberg. No SpaceX launch is scheduled today.

stories.headline: Rocket Lab’s 98th Electron puts three HawkEye 360 satellites in orbit
stories.body: Rocket Lab launched “We’re Not Hawking Around” from New Zealand, placing three radio-signal-tracking satellites in a 520-kilometer orbit. It was Rocket Lab’s 19th launch of 2026, with the 100th Electron flight now in sight.

stories.headline: Starship Flight 15 targets Nov. 8 with two catches planned
stories.body: SpaceX aims to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the ship on Flight 15. A ship catch would be a first and is central to making Starship fully reusable, which NASA’s 2028 lunar landing plans depend on.

stories.headline: China’s Guowang network keeps growing
stories.body: Saturday’s Long March 8A from Hainan added nine satellites to Guowang, China’s state broadband answer to Starlink; it was the 674th Long March flight. Next on the U.S. side: Starlink 15-18 from Vandenberg early Friday.

stories.headline: Thursday’s spacewalk: Menon and Kutryk to install a new solar array
stories.body: NASA’s Anil Menon and Canada’s Joshua Kutryk step outside Thursday at 8 a.m. Eastern, with NASA+ coverage from 6:30, to install a roll-out solar array on the station’s port truss. Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney will assist from inside. The crew also packed a failed robot-arm wrist joint to ride home on a Dragon in November.

stories.headline: Artemis III: SLS core stage joins the boosters this week
stories.body: NASA said its core stage would be stacked between the twin boosters this week in the Vehicle Assembly Building. A shortened “stubby” stack will do fueling tests to fix past hydrogen leaks, and a stretched Centaur V is the chosen future upper stage. stories.body: At his installation, Bishop Crispin Varquez urged tourism that protects Bohol’s environment, workers and heritage, and told his people, “Allow me to love you.” Who he is: a Tagbilaran native, bishop of Borongan for 19 years through Typhoon Yolanda, now the diocese’s eighth bishop, with the motto “Humility and Simplicity.” Cardinal Jose Advincula preached, and about 50 bishops attended.

stories.headline: Europe: Sicily buries Cardinal Paolo Romeo today
stories.body: Who he was: a priest of Acireale who became a Vatican diplomat, nuncio in Haiti, Colombia, Canada and Italy, then archbishop of Palermo from 2006 to 2015; Benedict XVI made him a cardinal in 2010. He died Sunday at 88.

stories.headline: Latin America: The Pope will meet abuse survivors on his trip
stories.body: The Nov. 6–17 visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru now includes a meeting with survivors, as Montevideo, Luján, Chiclayo and Cuzco prepare.

stories.headline: Appointments this week: Madagascar, Joliet, Italy and Greece
stories.body: Archbishop Jean Nicolas Rakotojaona now leads Fianarantsoa, Madagascar; born in 1973 with a theology doctorate from Fribourg, he was coadjutor until Sunday. Bishop Brendan Cahill, until now bishop of Victoria, Texas, is installed in Joliet on Nov. 11. Thursday, Giorgio Ferretti takes possession of Lucera-Troia in Italy; Saturday, Georgios Altouvas is installed at Syros in Greece, and Michele Di Tolve, a Milan priest, at Chioggia.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Countdown Oct. 27; Medjugorje Oct. 25; Africa’s Church rising.

stories.headline: Countdown to the Kingdom: latest post Oct. 27, on the Divine Will
stories.body: Checked this morning, the newest post is Tuesday, Oct. 27: “How to Offer Your Ordinary Acts in the Divine Will,” in which Deacon Mike McKeown draws on Servant of God Luisa Piccarreta: before ordinary tasks, say interiorly, “Jesus wants to do this in me.” Before it: Marija’s Oct. 25 Medjugorje message, two Oct. 23 essays, “The Suicide of the West” and “Defending Your Family,” and Oct. 20 and 21 messages attributed to Pedro Regis in Brazil about “a great war” and “the one who opposes Christ.” The site asks readers to test every message with the Church, which alone judges authenticity.

stories.headline: Medjugorje, Oct. 25 (latest): “Pray more strongly and more for the peace”
stories.body: The latest monthly message, given Oct. 25, 2026, through Marija: “A fire of hatred and wars is spreading in the hearts of people who do not want peace but their own weak interests. That is why, little children, you be prayer and my extended hands of love and peace for all those who are far from my motherly heart. Pray more strongly and more for the peace that God desires to give you but you do not want it. I am with you and I am praying that peace may prevail and reign in every heart.” The next monthly message is due Nov. 25.

stories.headline: Reading the night beside the message
stories.body: Overnight brought both halves of the message. The fire: 88 drones over Ukraine, a missile on Saudi Arabia’s largest refinery claimed by the Houthis, talk of new strikes on Iran, and a UN warning that Sudan’s sieges could repeat El Fasher. The “extended hands”: 30 calm hours in Oleshky, Ethiopia’s and Eritrea’s leaders in the same city, Gulf states drafting a peace deal, and a Pope back in the square saying faith must become culture. The call is the same: pray more, and be peace where we are.

stories.headline: Missions: Africa’s Church overtakes Europe’s
stories.body: Fides counts 288 million Catholics in Africa, now more than in Europe, with Africa the only continent where seminarians increased. For a Church once evangelized by European missionaries, it is a striking reversal. Its bishops say the next test is sustaining that growth honestly, with budgets, audits and local generosity.

stories.headline: Revival on campus: 35 baptized at Ohio State; UniteUS keeps moving
stories.body: Nearly 1,000 people came to Ohio State’s fall kickoff, where 35 were baptized. UniteUS, which began at Auburn in 2023, reported more than 700 decisions for Christ and about 100 baptisms, some in plastic-lined truck beds, at Appalachian State, and held a campus night at South Alabama Tuesday; Belmont in Nashville is next, on Nov. 10. Local churches, not one big organization, are carrying much of this.

stories.headline: Eucharistic: Guatemala’s Cuilapa Host still under study
stories.body: In Cuilapa, a consecrated Host that witnesses say stayed intact in water for eight days and developed reddish stains is being examined by a multidisciplinary team. The diocese stresses only the Holy See can authorize veneration; cases like Sokółka in Poland took years of review.

stories.headline: Digital money, soberly: the digital euro pilot signs up merchants
stories.body: The European Central Bank’s deadline for merchants to apply for its digital euro pilot closed Oct. 27. The 12-month pilot is planned from late 2027, while lawmakers still argue over offline payments, anti-money-laundering rules and fees. In Britain, the national ID card is scrapped but the government digital wallet goes on. These are real systems worth watching closely, with privacy the key question, not cause for panic.

newAtThisHour.body: Likud stays the largest party; coalition talks could take weeks.

beats.title: World
beats.headline: Pope: no holy war; Israel exit polls split; Oleshky truce holds.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Pope Leo to Assisi: “There is no such thing as a holy war”
stories.body: In a video message played for religious leaders closing Sant’Egidio’s Assisi meeting, Pope Leo said war “can never be waged in the name of God” and that “only peace is holy.” He warned of a “troubling revival of war as an instrument of international politics” and said, “We must rebuild peace everywhere, not prepare for more wars.” He called prayer “the humble strength of believers” and asked God to make all believers “unarmed instruments of His peace.” He had hoped to be at Saint Francis’s tomb but is still recovering from his Oct. 13 surgery.
stories.why: It is the Pope’s clearest word yet on the wars in Ukraine, the Gulf and Africa, and it quotes his new encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, on religion and violence.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Pope will meet abuse survivors on his South America trip
stories.body: The Vatican said Tuesday that Pope Leo will meet survivors of clergy sexual abuse during his Nov. 6–17 journey to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. A senior Vatican official also told the AP that the Pope’s cancer diagnosis is a “game-changer” for how the papacy is seen, even as his recovery goes well and the full trip stands.
stories.why: Peru, where he served for years, has had its own painful abuse cases, so the meeting will be watched closely there.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Cardinal Paolo Romeo’s funeral is Wednesday in Acireale
stories.body: The funeral of Cardinal Paolo Romeo, Palermo’s archbishop from 2006 to 2015 and a longtime papal diplomat, is Wednesday at 11 a.m. Rome time in the cathedral of Acireale, his home diocese. He died Sunday at 88. His death leaves the College of Cardinals one member smaller ahead of any future consistory.

stories.headline: Africa: Ebola passes 10,000 confirmed cases, fastest-growing outbreak on record
stories.body: Congo now counts 10,060 confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases and 4,887 deaths across 66 health zones in eight provinces, the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and the deadliest Congo has seen. There is still no approved vaccine or treatment for this strain; the Tumaini trial, which vaccinated its first volunteer in Bunia on Oct. 23, is testing Ervebo first. Cases have also turned up in Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, France and the Netherlands.
stories.why: Nearly half of those infected have died, and the trial results, months away, are the main hope of bending the curve.

stories.headline: Africa: Sudan’s army steps up airstrikes as El Fasher stays under RSF control
stories.body: A year after El Fasher fell, the army has intensified air and drone strikes on Rapid Support Forces positions around the city and in West Kordofan, including Babanusa, while the RSF digs in at Nuhud. The UN says drone strikes killed at least 306 people in three weeks this month. Fewer than 70,000 people remain in El Fasher, Amnesty reports, facing detention, torture and little aid.

stories.headline: Africa: Ethiopia holds Tigray’s cities; fears grow of war with Eritrea
stories.body: Federal forces hold Tigray’s main cities, from Mekele and Aksum to Shire, while Tigrayan fighters hold out in the mountains and strike supply roads; they retook the border town of Rama after troops moved south. Eritrean troops are reported pulling back toward the border, though Asmara denies heavy losses. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed warns Eritrea of “extremely severe consequences” for backing rebels, and Asmara accuses him of eyeing its Red Sea coast. The TPLF rejects Addis Ababa’s six-month caretaker administration; Washington, London and the African Union urge talks, and Eritrea has reportedly asked Kenya to mediate.
stories.why: The 2020–22 Tigray war killed an estimated 600,000 people; a wider war would also threaten Red Sea shipping.

stories.headline: Asia: Israel’s exit polls rebuke Netanyahu, but no one has 61 seats
stories.body: Exit polls from Israel’s three main channels give the anti-Netanyahu parties about 52 seats to 50 for his bloc, with Arab-led parties projected at a record 18. Likud is still the largest party at 24 to 25 seats, ahead of Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar at 21 to 23. The easiest path to a new government would have Eisenkot rely on Arab-led parties, which could split the opposition, so weeks of bargaining are likely. Election day saw a man arrested after apparently trying to stab Democrats leader Yair Golan; official results are due Nov. 4.
stories.why: Who governs Israel will shape any deal with Iran, the Gaza aftermath and the U.S. decision on renewed strikes.

stories.headline: Asia: Houthi missiles explode over Riyadh as Tehran talks end without a deal
stories.body: Saudi authorities said they destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles over Riyadh on Tuesday and three more aimed at the Eastern Province, with shrapnel causing limited damage in the capital. The talks in Tehran between Iran and the Mecca pact nations of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan ended with an agreement to keep talking but no pledge to stop the Houthi attacks. In Yemen, the UN says about 280,000 people have been displaced since August, nearly half of them from Taiz.

stories.headline: Asia: Cyclone Arnab begins landfall in Andhra Pradesh
stories.body: Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Arnab began crossing India’s Andhra Pradesh coast near Narsapur, south of Yanam, early Wednesday local time, which is Tuesday afternoon Eastern, with sustained winds of 125 to 135 km/h and gusts to 150. Visakhapatnam was battered by rain, flights were cancelled, and more than 130,000 people had been evacuated in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

stories.headline: Europe: The Oleshky truce holds and will run until Sunday night
stories.body: Both sides observed the local ceasefire in occupied Oleshky through Tuesday, Ukraine’s human rights commissioner said, and Russia’s Defense Ministry confirmed it halted fire in the Kherson sector. Ukrainian lawmaker David Arakhamia said it lasts until late Nov. 1 and called it “the largest de-escalation since 2022.” Mines must be cleared before 1,700 to 2,000 mostly elderly residents can leave, and Zelenskyy warns Russia may steer evacuees toward its own territory. Fighting and strikes go on everywhere else.
stories.why: The truce followed Pope Leo’s direct plea to Putin a week earlier, and diplomats hope it can become a template before talks resume in November.

stories.headline: Europe: Overnight, 16 ballistic missiles and 280 drones hit Kyiv’s bridge
stories.body: Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones overnight, mainly at Kyiv, Zelenskyy said. A 46-year-old woman was killed and about 15 people hurt, most of them students in a university dormitory. Strikes damaged the Pivdennyi Bridge, a key Dnipro crossing that carries a metro line, and it stays closed. Zelenskyy called it a “serious escalation” against logistics and said delays to Patriot and NASAMS interceptors “directly help Russia.”

stories.headline: Europe: Ukraine’s €70 billion gap strains the EU budget; gas prices triple
stories.body: Brussels is trying to fill a 70-billion-euro gap in Ukraine’s funding while it fights over the next long-term EU budget. European gas prices have tripled this year and storage is at a record low going into winter. In lighter news, Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or, the first Englishman in 25 years, after 61 goals in 51 games.

stories.headline: North America: The President stumps in Texas and won’t pledge to accept results
stories.body: The President made his third trip to Texas, rallying in Corpus Christi and Lubbock for Senate candidate Ken Paxton and Governor Greg Abbott in a close race with Democrat James Talarico. He told reporters he will accept the midterm results only if the elections are “honest.” A new NPR poll gives Democrats an edge, with caution signs, and the AP reports the Iran standoff and higher gas prices are weighing on Republican hopes.

stories.headline: North America: Appeals court rejects bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots
stories.body: A Ninth Circuit panel turned down the Justice Department’s emergency request to make California set aside ballots from 20,000 people it says are noncitizens. In Alaska, a federal judge fast-tracked a DOJ suit that could affect certifying the Senate race because two candidates named Sullivan are on the ballot. She could rule by week’s end. The President also offered a $1 million reward for voter-fraud tips that lead to a conviction, though studies find such fraud rare.

stories.headline: North America: More than 30 million early votes, a week from Election Day
stories.body: More than 30 million Americans have voted early, several days ahead of the 2022 pace. Late Monday in Corinth, Mississippi, the President campaigned for Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in a state he won by 23 points: “I can’t take a chance.” Vice President Vance was in Kansas for Senator Roger Marshall, and Republicans rallied in South Carolina for Senator Darline Graham. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3.

stories.headline: South America: Brazil’s two-hour extension was a tiny fraction of Lula’s margin
stories.body: Flávio Bolsonaro still refuses to concede, blaming the Supreme Court’s order to keep polls open until 7 p.m. But voting-machine logs show only 35,521 votes were cast after 5 p.m., less than 1 percent of Lula’s winning margin of more than 4 million. The heads of the Supreme Court, the electoral court and both houses of Congress have recognized the result, and Argentina’s Milei is staying silent.

stories.headline: South America: Rubio tells Machado street protests won’t bring democracy
stories.body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington told Venezuelan officials “weeks and weeks ago” that María Corina Machado should be allowed home, but he urged a negotiated transition rather than street protests. Machado returned overland from Colombia on Oct. 25 to crowds along the road to Caracas, and her return is adding pressure on U.S.-backed talks over judicial and electoral reforms. Acting president Delcy Rodríguez has called the homecoming a “show,” and no election date is set.

stories.headline: South America: More than 300 U.S. soldiers arrive in Colombia for drug-war training
stories.body: U.S. troops arrive today at Tolemaida, Colombia’s largest base, for the Vanguardia del Sur exercise through Nov. 11, focused on counternarcotics, illegal mining, drones and medical evacuation. Petro’s former party says Congress must authorize it, but the government says training missions don’t need that permission.

stories.headline: Oceania: Security boost for MPs after the Haines attack; first AUKUS sub named
stories.body: Prime Minister Albanese says a review of politicians’ security will be fast-tracked after independent MP Helen Haines lost both legs in an alleged car attack. The U.S. named the USS Colorado, a 10-year-old Virginia-class submarine, as the first to be based in Western Australia under AUKUS, from late 2027. Senator Jacqui Lambie objected that the used boats come without a warranty.

stories.headline: Oceania: A magnitude 4.9 quake rattles Adelaide
stories.body: A magnitude 4.9 earthquake struck offshore south of Victor Harbor just before 8 a.m. local time, felt across the Adelaide Hills, the Fleurieu Peninsula and the Murraylands. No serious damage was reported.

stories.headline: Oceania: AI-driven cyberattacks up 20 percent; New Zealand votes early
stories.body: Australia’s Signals Directorate counted about 1,500 cyber incidents last year, up 20 percent, with medium-sized businesses hit hardest as criminals use AI. Across the Tasman, New Zealand’s advance voting is in its second day before the Nov. 7 election.

beats.title: MAGA / MAHA promises kept
beats.headline: Breast cancer screening push; Oleshky truce holds; “honest” elections.

stories.headline: MAHA: HHS launches a breast cancer screening push
stories.body: Promise: focus on prevention and early detection. Action: HHS announced a coordinated effort to study national screening patterns, spread proven practices through more than 40 health systems, and speed follow-up after abnormal mammograms, plus a partnership with DenseBreast-info.org on breast-density education. Impact: the hospital association welcomed it; the measure that matters is how many women get timely follow-up, which HHS has not yet put numbers on.

stories.headline: Ending the Ukraine war: the Oleshky truce holds on day one
stories.body: Promise: end the war. Action: the First Lady’s local truce in Oleshky took effect at 3 a.m. Kyiv time and both sides observed it through Tuesday; it runs until late Sunday. Impact: aid and evacuation can start once roads are de-mined. Supporters call it the biggest de-escalation since 2022; skeptics note Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv the same night.

stories.headline: Election integrity: “honest” elections, or no promise to accept results
stories.body: Promise: secure elections. Action: the President said he will accept the midterm results if they are “honest,” while the Justice Department presses challenges in California and Alaska. Impact: supporters say he is guarding against fraud; critics say the conditional pledge undermines trust a week before the vote.

stories.headline: Lower gas prices: $150 million in Defense Production Act money for refineries
stories.body: Promise: cheaper fuel. Action: the White House is using the Defense Production Act to release 150 million dollars to expand U.S. refining, under an Oct. 22 order that also covers pipelines, storage and terminals. Impact: new refining capacity takes years, while prices now depend on the Iran war and Hormuz. Iran claims it has the strait “completely closed.” Supporters call it a long-term fix, and critics say it does little before the Nov. 3 vote.

stories.headline: MAHA: kidney and dementia plans, from a Florida swing
stories.body: Promise: confront chronic disease. Action: on a four-day tour of Texas and Florida, including Fort Lauderdale and Miami, Secretary Kennedy announced a National Kidney Plan with up to 4.67 million dollars in prizes and a 10-year national plan on Alzheimer’s. He also pushed for 40 hours of nutrition training in medical school. He is in Detroit today on homelessness and addiction. Impact: mostly plans and pledges so far; results will take years to measure.

stories.headline: MAHA, room for disagreement: food rules are delayed and an adviser leaves
stories.body: Axios reports “zero” sign that Kennedy plans to leave HHS after the midterms, and the White House praises his record. But top MAHA advocate Calley Means resigned last week, reportedly frustrated by slow progress on food. Rules defining ultraprocessed foods and improving school meals have been put off, and some of the agenda is frozen in court. Supporters see a movement reshaping health policy, and critics inside MAHA say it is losing momentum.

stories.headline: Peace through strength: forces ready, decision deferred
stories.body: Promise: stop Iran’s nuclear program. Action: CNN reports U.S. forces could launch a major operation within 96 hours of an order, but the President has not decided and has said nothing will happen before the midterms. Impact: Gulf neighbors are now talking directly with Tehran. Supporters see that as pressure working, and critics point to the Houthi missiles and the closed strait.

beats.title: Musk world
beats.headline: Tesla tops $400 again; merger committees face scrutiny.

stories.headline: Tesla: up another 4 percent to about $407 on merger hopes
stories.body: Tesla closed near 407 dollars, up about 4 percent, building on Monday’s 5 percent jump after Barclays’ upgrade. Investing.com notes sell ratings on Tesla are at their lowest in about 11 years, and Latvia became the tenth EU country to approve Full Self-Driving. Bloomberg reports that the independent committees weighing a SpaceX merger are made up of directors with close Musk ties, which could draw shareholder scrutiny; a Tesla deal would need a majority of all outstanding shares.
stories.why: Two straight days of gains put the stock back above 400 dollars, but the merger is not agreed and no structure has been disclosed.

stories.headline: SpaceX: shares near $147 after a $40 billion AI-chip financing
stories.body: SpaceX, trading as SPCX, closed Monday at 146.90 dollars, down 0.4 percent, for a market value near 2 trillion dollars. The stock’s 52-week range runs from about 105 to 226 dollars. Musk confirmed a roughly 40-billion-dollar Apollo-backed debt deal to lease AI chips from early 2027 for SpaceX’s AI unit, the former xAI. He said many smaller AI cloud providers will fail and SpaceX will not buy them.

stories.headline: Starlink: overnight launch adds 27 satellites
stories.body: A Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg at 3:25 a.m. Eastern with 27 Starlink satellites. Its booster, flying for the 26th time, landed on the drone ship Of Course I Still Love You. Starlink is SpaceX’s main source of revenue and pays for Starship.

stories.headline: Starlink in Ukraine: fast-platform service back on
stories.body: Service for platforms moving faster than 400 km/h, which matters for drones, has been restored, Ukraine’s defense ministry says. Kyiv rejects Musk’s claim that it broke Starlink’s terms. Musk says the US government controls changes to Starshield, the military version.

beats.title: Space
beats.headline: Starship Flight 15 eyes Nov. 8; Starlink launch overnight.

stories.headline: Starship Flight 15 targets Nov. 8 with two catches planned
stories.body: NASASpaceflight reports SpaceX is working through milestones for Starship Flights 15 and 16, with Flight 15 targeted for Nov. 8 and plans to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the ship. Overnight’s Falcon 9 from Vandenberg put 27 more Starlink satellites in orbit, and booster B1082 landed on the droneship Of Course I Still Love You.

stories.headline: Overnight: Starlink 15-16 flies on a 26th-flight booster
stories.body: SpaceX launched 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 3:25 a.m. Eastern into a 70-degree orbit. Booster B1082, in service since January 2024, has also flown national-security and OneWeb missions, and this was its 26th flight.

stories.headline: China’s Guowang network grows with nine more satellites
stories.body: Saturday night’s Long March 8A from Hainan added nine satellites to Guowang, China’s state broadband network and its answer to Starlink. It was the 674th flight of the Long March family. China is building two megaconstellations at once, and launch cadence is the bottleneck.

beats.title: NASA
beats.headline: UVEX telescope approved; Mars-sim crew exits Halloween.

stories.headline: NASA approves UVEX, an ultraviolet telescope to map the whole sky
stories.body: NASA confirmed the Caltech-led UVEX mission, committing to launch by January 2031 at a lifecycle cost of 590 million dollars. It will make the first deep ultraviolet maps of the entire sky, studying young stars, galaxies and the flashes from colliding neutron stars.

stories.headline: Four volunteers leave NASA’s yearlong Mars habitat on Oct. 31
stories.body: The CHAPEA crew will step out of their 3D-printed Mars habitat in Houston on Halloween after 378 days of simulated Mars life. Aboard the station, the crew kept preparing for Thursday’s spacewalk to install a roll-out solar array, and NASA praised the Alabama-built SLS rocket as Artemis III moves ahead.

stories.headline: Swift’s mission ends after 20 years; reentry expected within weeks
stories.body: NASA has formally ended the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory after Katalyst’s robotic rescue craft failed to boost it. Swift was built for two years and lasted almost 22. It caught more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and 1,400 supernovae, and its data fed about 7,000 papers. It took its last data Oct. 20 and should fall back into the atmosphere in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: “More missions, more often”: NASA overhauls how it picks science missions
stories.body: Under Competition Model 2.0, ordered by Administrator Jared Isaacman, early proposals will focus on scientific merit, and detailed engineering and costing come later. Discovery and New Frontiers selections drop from 35 months to about 19.5, and the smallest missions move to a single round. There are tougher penalties for cost overruns, up to cancellation.

stories.headline: Perseverance measures the Mars dust astronauts will breathe
stories.body: JPL says Perseverance found Martian dust fine enough to reach deep into the lungs, data that will shape suits, habitats and filters for future crews.

beats.title: Catholic
beats.headline: Pope: “only peace is holy”; survivors’ meeting set for trip.

stories.headline: Miami: Archbishop Wenski at Jericho 2026: “God gave us our dignity”
stories.body: Celebrating his 76th birthday at Notre Dame d’Haïti in Little Haiti, Archbishop Thomas Wenski preached in Haitian Creole at the opening of Jericho, the mission’s week of renewal. “It is not TPS or a green card that gives us dignity,” he said; “God made us human.” He named walls of pride, indifference and fear, and the fear of ICE, to be torn down by prayer and the Word, not violence. Haiti’s TPS ended in July and legal challenges continue.

stories.headline: Miami: The archdiocese holds firm on school vaccine rules
stories.body: Archbishop Wenski continues to resist Attorney General James Uthmeier’s pressure over religious exemptions in Catholic schools, calling it “bullying” and defending vaccination as serving the common good.

stories.headline: Europe: “Only peace is holy,” the Pope tells Assisi
stories.body: The 40th-anniversary prayer for peace closed in Assisi with the Pope’s video message, which rejected every religious justification for war and called religious leaders to replace “the language of arrogance” with “the language of peace, negotiation and understanding.” He thanked Sant’Egidio and the Dicastery for Interreligious Dialogue for keeping Saint John Paul II’s 1986 initiative alive.

stories.headline: Latin America: Survivors’ meeting added to the Pope’s trip
stories.body: The Vatican says the Pope will meet clergy abuse survivors during the Nov. 6–17 visit, as Montevideo, Luján, Chiclayo, where he was bishop, and Cuzco prepare.

stories.headline: Asia: Bishop Crispin Varquez installed in his hometown, Tagbilaran
stories.body: Bishop Crispin “Bai” Varquez took possession of the Diocese of Tagbilaran in Bohol, Philippines, this morning as its eighth bishop, urging “passion and enthusiasm for the work of evangelization.” Who he is: a Tagbilaran native, 65, ordained in 1989, a former seminary formator, and bishop of Borongan in Eastern Samar from 2007. He succeeds Alberto Uy, now archbishop of Cebu.

stories.headline: Africa: Kidnapped Nigerian priest freed in Benue
stories.body: Fr. John Inalegwu Otache, pastor of St. Margaret’s in Ajegbe-Awume, was rescued with seven other captives by Benue police and local vigilantes, and two suspects were arrested. The Diocese of Otukpo gave thanks “with hearts full of joy” and asked prayers for those still held, including Fr. Emmanuel Ezema of Zaria, missing since December.

stories.headline: Middle East: Jordan answers the Karak church attack with strikes in Syria
stories.body: After Friday’s attack on a funeral at St. George Orthodox Church in Hamoud, Jordan struck Islamic State targets in southern Syria and says it killed more than 20 fighters. Syria reports eight civilian deaths. Pope Leo prayed for the victims at Sunday’s Angelus.

stories.headline: North America: New York’s $800 million abuse settlement nears signing
stories.body: The Archdiocese of New York and about 1,300 survivors agreed to an 800-million-dollar settlement, to be signed the week of Nov. 6. Archbishop Ronald Hicks prayed it would “bring some measure of healing and reconciliation.”

stories.headline: Appointments this week: Madagascar, Joliet, Italy and Greece
stories.body: Archbishop Jean Nicolas Rakotojaona now leads Fianarantsoa, Madagascar. He was born in 1973, holds a theology doctorate from Fribourg and was coadjutor until Sunday. Bishop Brendan Cahill, until now bishop of Victoria, Texas, will be installed in Joliet on Nov. 11. Thursday, Giorgio Ferretti takes possession of Lucera-Troia in Italy. Saturday, Georgios Altouvas is installed at Syros in Greece, and Michele Di Tolve, a Milan priest, at Chioggia.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Countdown Oct. 27; Medjugorje Oct. 25; Assisi says pray.

stories.headline: Countdown to the Kingdom: new post Oct. 27 on the Divine Will
stories.body: Checked this evening, the newest post is Tuesday, Oct. 27: “How to Offer Your Ordinary Acts in the Divine Will.” In it Deacon Mike McKeown draws on Servant of God Luisa Piccarreta’s writings to suggest a simple practice: before ordinary tasks, say interiorly, “Jesus wants to do this in me,” with a morning offering and an evening review. Before it came Marija’s Oct. 25 Medjugorje message, “A Fire of Hatred is Spreading,” and two Oct. 23 essays. The site asks readers to test every message with the Church, which alone judges authenticity.
stories.why: After two days of messages about war, the newest post turns to something anyone can do at the kitchen sink: offer the day’s small acts to God.

stories.headline: Medjugorje, Oct. 25 (latest): “Pray more strongly and more for the peace”
stories.body: The latest monthly message, given Oct. 25, 2026, through the visionary Marija: “Dear children! A fire of hatred and wars is spreading in the hearts of people who do not want peace but their own weak interests. That is why, little children, you be prayer and my extended hands of love and peace for all those who are far from my motherly heart. Pray more strongly and more for the peace that God desires to give you but you do not want it. I am with you and I am praying that peace may prevail and reign in every heart.” The next monthly message is due Nov. 25.

stories.headline: The message, the night’s news, and Assisi’s answer
stories.body: In the 48 hours since Our Lady spoke of a “fire of hatred and wars,” 16 ballistic missiles fell on Kyiv, Houthi missiles burst over Riyadh, and El Fasher marked a year under the RSF. Yet the same day brought a holding truce in Oleshky and Pope Leo’s word to Assisi that “only peace is holy” and that prayer, though it may seem weak, “is never in vain.” The message asks the same two things: be prayer, and be “extended hands of love and peace.”

stories.headline: Revival on campus: UniteUS at South Alabama tonight
stories.body: UniteUS, the student outreach that began at Auburn in 2023, holds its next campus night tonight at the University of South Alabama. At Appalachian State this month it reported more than 700 decisions for Christ and about 100 baptisms. The ministry says it has reached more than two dozen campuses, the University of Miami among them, and more than 100,000 students. Belmont in Nashville is next, on Nov. 10.

stories.headline: Revival by the water: beach and campus baptisms keep spreading
stories.body: More than 550 people were baptized at Bridlington South Beach in England on Oct. 10, after earlier beach baptisms at Bigbury. Thousands joined the oceanfront baptisms at Oceanside, California, on Oct. 17. Local churches report students baptized after campus nights from Mississippi to Georgia. Many of these gatherings are led by local congregations, not one big organization.

stories.headline: Eucharistic: Guatemala’s Cuilapa Host under study
stories.body: Witnesses in Cuilapa, Guatemala, describe a consecrated Host that stayed intact in water for eight days and developed reddish stains. A multidisciplinary team is studying it, and the diocese stresses that only the Holy See can authorize veneration. Similar cases, such as Sokółka in Poland, took years of scientific and Church review.

stories.headline: Digital ID, soberly: Britain dropped the scheme but kept the plumbing
stories.body: Britain has scrapped its national digital ID card, the compulsory-then-voluntary plan that Prime Minister Andy Burnham ended. But officials told MPs that One Login and the government digital wallet continue, with more than 80 credential types planned and digital driving licences targeted for 2027. One MP warned of digital ID “by the back door.” In Europe, the digital euro is still being negotiated, with a pilot planned for late 2027 and possible issuance in 2029. It is real infrastructure that deserves scrutiny, not panic.

stories.body: Wednesday at 6 p.m. Miami-Dade Schools Police holds a free trunk-or-treat at 3300 NW 27th Ave. Thursday from 4 to 8, Hialeah Cares throws a free Halloween party and haunted house at Miami Dade College Hialeah. On Friday, The Berry Farm hosts Boo at the Patch from 3 p.m. Saturday brings Trick-or-Treat on the Mile in Coral Gables from 2 to 6, Frost Science’s Spooky Science Monster Mash from 11 to 3, and Tidal Cove’s “Tidal-ween.”

stories.headline: Thursday: VOUS Worship’s “Man Alive,” free at Bayfront Park
stories.body: VOUS Worship brings “Man Alive” to the FPL Solar Amphitheater at Bayfront Park on Thursday, Oct. 29. Doors open at 6, music runs 7 to 10, and admission is free.

stories.headline: Next week and beyond: Crowder, Miles Minnick, Gilberto Daza, Jekalyn Carr

beats.headline: Heat at Atlanta Wednesday; Episode X casting reports.

stories.headline: Heat: 0–4 after Giannis’s triple-double; Atlanta Wednesday at 7
stories.body: Giannis Antetokounmpo had 29 points, 15 rebounds and 11 assists, his first triple-double with the Heat, and Davion Mitchell scored 21. But Cooper Flagg had 29 points and 11 assists, and with 31 seconds left he blocked Andrew Wiggins’s three that would have put Miami ahead. Dallas won 113–109. At 0–4, the Heat are off to their worst start since 2008–09. Next: at Atlanta Wednesday at 7, then Indiana at home Friday at 8.
stories.why: In 2008–09, the Heat started 0–4 and still made the playoffs.

stories.headline: Star Wars: Episode X reportedly centers on two new leads
stories.body: ComicBook.com reports casting details for Star Wars: Episode X point to two new lead characters, with Daisy Ridley’s Rey in a supporting, mentoring role. Lucasfilm has not confirmed the report. Meanwhile, a new comic, Smugglers and Scoundrels: The Black Sun Eclipse, picks up Han and Lando two years after Solo.

stories.headline: Star Wars: Ahsoka Season 2 trailer brings back Hayden Christensen’s Anakin
stories.body: The new trailer, shown at D23, sets Ahsoka Season 2 for Jan. 20, 2027 on Disney+. Anakin returns as a Force ghost and in Clone Wars flashbacks, asking Ahsoka: “Are you a Jedi... or not?” Sabine trains with Ahsoka on Peridea, Ezra fights Death Troopers, and Rory McCann takes over as Baylan Skoll. Dave Filoni says the Mortis gods are “definitely a thing.”

stories.headline: Star Wars: Vader’s Monday Night Football interviews begin
stories.body: An animated Darth Vader began interviewing NFL players on Monday Night Football, building to an all-animated Star Wars telecast of the Super Bowl on Feb. 14, 2027. Next Tuesday, Nov. 3, the 256-page art book for The Mandalorian and Grogu arrives.

beats.title: World
beats.headline: Kyiv bridge hit; Israel votes; Pope’s Assisi peace message today.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Pope Leo sends his peace message to Assisi today
stories.body: Religious leaders close Sant’Egidio’s three-day “Unarmed and Disarming Peace” meeting in Assisi this afternoon, 40 years to the day after Saint John Paul II’s first World Day of Prayer for Peace. Pope Leo will not be there: his doctors advised against the helicopter trip so soon after his Oct. 13 lung surgery. Instead his message will be read at the prayer in the Lower Basilica of Saint Francis, where Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew also speaks. Some 384 delegates from 53 countries took part.
stories.why: The meeting’s theme comes from the Pope’s own book on peace, so today’s text will be read as a programmatic word on war, from Ukraine to the Gulf.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Recovery on track, South America trip still set for Nov. 6
stories.body: A day after doctors cleared him to travel, the plan holds: Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov. 6 to 17, including Cuzco above 11,000 feet. Surgeons say the cancer removed on Oct. 13 was localized and needs no further treatment, and a follow-up X-ray showed recovery “progressing very well.” The Pope has kept a light schedule, resuming audiences gradually since leaving hospital.

stories.headline: Vatican City: Cardinal Paolo Romeo’s funeral is Wednesday in Acireale
stories.body: The funeral of Cardinal Paolo Romeo, Palermo’s archbishop from 2006 to 2015 and a longtime papal diplomat, is Wednesday at 11 a.m. Rome time in the cathedral of Acireale, his home diocese. He died Sunday at 88. His death leaves the College of Cardinals one member smaller ahead of any future consistory.

stories.headline: Africa: Congo’s Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases as vaccine trial begins
stories.body: Congo’s government says the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has passed 10,000 confirmed cases, with nearly half of those infected dying, across eight provinces. There is still no approved vaccine for this strain. On Oct. 23 the first volunteer was vaccinated in Bunia in Tumaini, a trial named for the Swahili word for “hope,” testing Ervebo first, with Moderna and Oxford candidates to follow. Kenya’s nine cases remain in one cluster, and M23-held areas of the Kivus remain the hardest places to trace contacts.
stories.why: This is now the second-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded; a working vaccine would change the response.

stories.headline: Africa: One year after El Fasher fell, the RSF still holds Darfur’s capital
stories.body: Human Rights Watch marked the anniversary with a stark account: an 18-month siege, a trench dug around the city, and more than 6,000 people killed in three days when the Rapid Support Forces took it, by the UN’s estimate. UN investigators say the campaign bore the “hallmarks of genocide.” Fewer than 70,000 people remain, facing detention and little aid, and RSF fighters have held up aid convoys. Washington is pushing to extend the Darfur arms embargo nationwide.

stories.headline: Africa: Ethiopia and Eritrea trade warnings as fighting moves into Tigray’s mountains
stories.body: Federal forces now hold Tigray’s main cities, from Mekele to Shire, and are pushing into the mountainous interior. Tigrayan fighters have struck back on supply roads, and they retook the border town of Rama after troops redeployed south. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed warns Eritrea of “extremely severe consequences” for backing rebels, and Asmara accuses him of eyeing its Red Sea coast. A six-month caretaker council is preparing regional elections. Washington, London and the African Union urge talks, and Eritrea has reportedly asked Kenya to mediate.
stories.why: The 2020–22 Tigray war killed an estimated 600,000 people; a wider war would also threaten Red Sea shipping.

stories.headline: Asia: Israel votes, with the highest early turnout since 1981
stories.body: Israelis are voting today in the first general election since Oct. 7, 2023. By 10 a.m. local time turnout stood at 16.7 percent, the highest at that hour since 1981. Final polls had Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party ahead of Likud, 22 seats to about 20, with neither bloc near 61. Exit polls come when polls close at 4 p.m. Eastern, but forming a government could take weeks.

stories.headline: Asia: Overnight, more Houthi missiles at Saudi Arabia; Jordan strikes Syria
stories.body: Saudi defenses intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the Eastern Province and four drones overnight, with no casualties. In Tehran, Iran and the Mecca pact nations of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan agreed to keep talking, but Iran still insists on seven conditions before any talks with Washington. CNN reports U.S. forces could launch a major operation within 96 hours of an order. Jordan says its strikes in southern Syria killed more than 20 Islamic State fighters after Friday’s church attack. Syria says eight civilians died, including three children, and has closed its main border crossing.

stories.headline: Asia: India evacuates more than 130,000 ahead of Cyclone Arnab
stories.body: Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Arnab is forecast to hit India’s Andhra Pradesh coast near Kakinada on Wednesday morning, with sustained winds up to 125 km/h. Andhra Pradesh is evacuating about 89,000 people and Odisha 48,000, while schools are closed and trains are cancelled. Nepal has warned trekkers of snowstorms and avalanches later this week.

stories.headline: Europe: Overnight, 16 ballistic missiles and 280 drones hit Kyiv’s bridge
stories.body: Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones overnight, mainly at Kyiv, Zelenskyy said. A 46-year-old woman was killed and about 15 people hurt, most of them students in a university dormitory. Strikes damaged the Pivdennyi Bridge, a key Dnipro crossing that carries a metro line, and it stays closed. Zelenskyy called it a “serious escalation” against logistics and said delays to Patriot and NASAMS interceptors “directly help Russia.”

stories.headline: Europe: Oleshky truce begins; Finland and Norway call Putin
stories.body: A local truce began early today in occupied Oleshky, across the Dnipro from Kherson, so aid can reach the 1,700 to 2,000 mostly elderly people left and those who want to leave can go. Melania Trump brokered the deal. This morning Finland’s President Alexander Stubb and Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre phoned Vladimir Putin, their first known call with him since early in the invasion, in consultation with Kyiv and ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi. Stubb called it “frank and substantive.”

stories.headline: Europe: Ukraine’s €70 billion gap strains the EU budget; gas prices triple
stories.body: Brussels is trying to fill a 70-billion-euro gap in Ukraine’s funding while it fights over the next long-term EU budget. European gas prices have tripled this year and storage is at a record low going into winter. In lighter news, Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or, the first Englishman in 25 years, after 61 goals in 51 games.

stories.headline: North America: More than 30 million early votes, a week from Election Day
stories.body: More than 30 million Americans have voted early, several days ahead of the 2022 pace. Late Monday in Corinth, Mississippi, the President campaigned for Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in a state he won by 23 points: “I can’t take a chance.” Vice President Vance was in Kansas for Senator Roger Marshall, and Republicans rallied in South Carolina for Senator Darline Graham. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3.

stories.headline: North America: Appeals court rejects bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots
stories.body: A Ninth Circuit panel turned down the Justice Department’s emergency request to make California set aside ballots from 20,000 people it says are noncitizens. In Alaska, a federal judge fast-tracked a DOJ suit that could affect certifying the Senate race because two candidates named Sullivan are on the ballot. She could rule by week’s end. The President also offered a $1 million reward for voter-fraud tips that lead to a conviction, though studies find such fraud rare.

stories.headline: North America: In Miami, the Heat fall to 0–4
stories.body: Closer to home, Cooper Flagg scored 29 and blocked Andrew Wiggins’s go-ahead three with 31 seconds left, and Dallas beat Miami 113–109 at a sold-out Kaseya Center. More in the Pick-me-up.

stories.headline: South America: Brazil’s two-hour extension was a tiny fraction of Lula’s margin
stories.body: Flávio Bolsonaro still refuses to concede, blaming the Supreme Court’s order to keep polls open until 7 p.m. But voting-machine logs show only 35,521 votes were cast after 5 p.m., less than 1 percent of Lula’s winning margin of more than 4 million. The heads of the Supreme Court, the electoral court and both houses of Congress have recognized the result, and Argentina’s Milei is staying silent.

stories.headline: South America: Delcy Rodríguez calls Machado’s homecoming a “show”
stories.body: Venezuela’s acting president urged María Corina Machado to drop the “show” and focus on dialogue, saying she hoped for “remorse and repentance” over Machado’s calls for sanctions. Machado’s party is still left out of government talks with other opposition groups, though she says she will not block them. No election date has been set.

stories.headline: South America: More than 300 U.S. soldiers arrive in Colombia for drug-war training
stories.body: U.S. troops arrive today at Tolemaida, Colombia’s largest base, for the Vanguardia del Sur exercise through Nov. 11, focused on counternarcotics, illegal mining, drones and medical evacuation. Petro’s former party says Congress must authorize it, but the government says training missions don’t need that permission.

stories.headline: Oceania: Security boost for MPs after the Haines attack; first AUKUS sub named
stories.body: Prime Minister Albanese says a review of politicians’ security will be fast-tracked after independent MP Helen Haines lost both legs in an alleged car attack. The U.S. named the USS Colorado, a 10-year-old Virginia-class submarine, as the first to be based in Western Australia under AUKUS, from late 2027. Senator Jacqui Lambie objected that the used boats come without a warranty.

stories.headline: Oceania: A magnitude 4.9 quake rattles Adelaide
stories.body: A magnitude 4.9 earthquake struck offshore south of Victor Harbor just before 8 a.m. local time, felt across the Adelaide Hills, the Fleurieu Peninsula and the Murraylands. No serious damage was reported.

stories.headline: Oceania: AI-driven cyberattacks up 20 percent; New Zealand votes early
stories.body: Australia’s Signals Directorate counted about 1,500 cyber incidents last year, up 20 percent, with medium-sized businesses hit hardest as criminals use AI. Across the Tasman, New Zealand’s advance voting is in its second day before the Nov. 7 election.

beats.title: MAGA / MAHA promises kept
beats.headline: Refinery money, kidney plan; Oleshky truce begins amid Kyiv strikes.

stories.headline: Lower gas prices: $150 million in Defense Production Act money for refineries
stories.body: Promise: cheaper fuel. Action: the White House is using the Defense Production Act to release 150 million dollars to expand U.S. refining, under an Oct. 22 order that also covers pipelines, storage and terminals. Impact: new refining capacity takes years, while prices now depend on the Iran war and Hormuz. Iran claims it has the strait “completely closed.” Supporters call it a long-term fix, and critics say it does little before the Nov. 3 vote.

stories.headline: MAHA: kidney and dementia plans, from a Florida swing
stories.body: Promise: confront chronic disease. Action: on a four-day tour of Texas and Florida, including Fort Lauderdale and Miami, Secretary Kennedy announced a National Kidney Plan with up to 4.67 million dollars in prizes and a 10-year national plan on Alzheimer’s. He also pushed for 40 hours of nutrition training in medical school. He is in Detroit today on homelessness and addiction. Impact: mostly plans and pledges so far; results will take years to measure.

stories.headline: MAHA, room for disagreement: food rules are delayed and an adviser leaves
stories.body: Axios reports “zero” sign that Kennedy plans to leave HHS after the midterms, and the White House praises his record. But top MAHA advocate Calley Means resigned last week, reportedly frustrated by slow progress on food. Rules defining ultraprocessed foods and improving school meals have been put off, and some of the agenda is frozen in court. Supporters see a movement reshaping health policy, and critics inside MAHA say it is losing momentum.

stories.headline: Ending the Ukraine war: a small truce begins as missiles hit Kyiv
stories.body: Promise: end the war. Action: the First Lady’s Oleshky truce took effect this morning, and three-way talks are set for Abu Dhabi in November. Impact: the same night, Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv, and Zelenskyy says Patriot deliveries are delayed. The truce is real relief for a town of about 2,000 mostly elderly people, but the wider war has not slowed.

stories.headline: Peace through strength: forces ready, decision deferred
stories.body: Promise: stop Iran’s nuclear program. Action: CNN reports U.S. forces could launch a major operation within 96 hours of an order, but the President has not decided and has said nothing will happen before the midterms. Impact: Gulf neighbors are now talking directly with Tehran. Supporters see that as pressure working, and critics point to the Houthi missiles and the closed strait.

stories.headline: Election integrity: courts push back as early voting surges
stories.body: Promise: secure elections. Action: a $1 million tip reward and lawsuits in California and Alaska. Impact: the Ninth Circuit rejected the California bid, and an Alaska judge sounded skeptical. Supporters call it vigilance, and critics, including California’s attorney general, call it groundwork to dispute losses. Meanwhile more than 30 million people have already voted.

beats.title: Musk world
beats.headline: Merger committees study Tesla-SpaceX; overnight Starlink launch.

stories.headline: Tesla: after Monday’s 5 percent jump, the merger talk intensifies
stories.body: Tesla closed Monday at 391.62 dollars, up 5.2 percent, after Barclays raised it to overweight with a 450-dollar target, making an expected SpaceX combination central to its bull case. Musk says special committees at both companies are studying a merger and that he is recused as a “conflicted party.” He called the subject “tap dancing through a minefield.” Shareholders would have to approve any deal, and regulators would take time. The stock is still down about 13 percent this year.
stories.why: For shareholders, the swap ratio in any deal matters more than the headline.

stories.headline: SpaceX: shares near $147 after a $40 billion AI-chip financing
stories.body: SpaceX, trading as SPCX, closed Monday at 146.90 dollars, down 0.4 percent, for a market value near 2 trillion dollars. The stock’s 52-week range runs from about 105 to 226 dollars. Musk confirmed a roughly 40-billion-dollar Apollo-backed debt deal to lease AI chips from early 2027 for SpaceX’s AI unit, the former xAI. He said many smaller AI cloud providers will fail and SpaceX will not buy them.

stories.headline: Starlink: overnight launch adds 27 satellites
stories.body: A Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg at 3:25 a.m. Eastern with 27 Starlink satellites. Its booster, flying for the 26th time, landed on the drone ship Of Course I Still Love You. Starlink is SpaceX’s main source of revenue and pays for Starship.

stories.headline: Starlink in Ukraine: fast-platform service back on
stories.body: Service for platforms moving faster than 400 km/h, which matters for drones, has been restored, Ukraine’s defense ministry says. Kyiv rejects Musk’s claim that it broke Starlink’s terms. Musk says the US government controls changes to Starshield, the military version.

beats.title: Space
beats.headline: Starlink 15-16 flies overnight; Guowang grows; Starship eyes November.

stories.headline: Overnight: Starlink 15-16 flies on a 26th-flight booster
stories.body: SpaceX launched 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 3:25 a.m. Eastern into a 70-degree orbit. Booster B1082, in service since January 2024, has also flown national-security and OneWeb missions, and this was its 26th flight.

stories.headline: China’s Guowang network grows with nine more satellites
stories.body: Saturday night’s Long March 8A from Hainan added nine satellites to Guowang, China’s state broadband network and its answer to Starlink. It was the 674th flight of the Long March family. China is building two megaconstellations at once, and launch cadence is the bottleneck.

stories.headline: Starship eyes November as launch capacity becomes the bottleneck
stories.body: Starship’s next flight is targeted for November. Starbase is seeking approval for up to 456 launches a year, and Blue Origin plans new Florida pads. Both moon landers need many refueling flights, so how often they can launch is now the key question for Artemis.

beats.title: NASA
beats.headline: Swift mission ends; NASA speeds science mission selection.

stories.headline: Swift’s mission ends after 20 years; reentry expected within weeks
stories.body: NASA has formally ended the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory after Katalyst’s robotic rescue craft failed to boost it. Swift was built for two years and lasted almost 22. It caught more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and 1,400 supernovae, and its data fed about 7,000 papers. It took its last data Oct. 20 and should fall back into the atmosphere in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: “More missions, more often”: NASA overhauls how it picks science missions
stories.body: Under Competition Model 2.0, ordered by Administrator Jared Isaacman, early proposals will focus on scientific merit, and detailed engineering and costing come later. Discovery and New Frontiers selections drop from 35 months to about 19.5, and the smallest missions move to a single round. There are tougher penalties for cost overruns, up to cancellation.

stories.headline: Station spacewalk Thursday; a moon-landing simulator opens to reporters
stories.body: The station crew is preparing for Thursday’s spacewalk to install a new roll-out solar array. NASA Ames shows reporters its lunar-landing simulator Oct. 29–30 as Artemis aims for a 2028 landing.

stories.headline: Perseverance measures the Mars dust astronauts will breathe
stories.body: JPL says Perseverance found Martian dust fine enough to reach deep into the lungs, data that will shape suits, habitats and filters for future crews.

beats.title: Catholic
beats.headline: Wenski on dignity; Varquez installed in Bohol; Nigerian priest freed.

stories.headline: Miami: Archbishop Wenski at Jericho 2026: “God gave us our dignity”
stories.body: Celebrating his 76th birthday at Notre Dame d’Haïti in Little Haiti, Archbishop Thomas Wenski preached in Haitian Creole at the opening of Jericho, the mission’s week of renewal. “It is not TPS or a green card that gives us dignity,” he said; “God made us human.” He named walls of pride, indifference and fear, and the fear of ICE, to be torn down by prayer and the Word, not violence. Haiti’s TPS ended in July and legal challenges continue.

stories.headline: Miami: The archdiocese holds firm on school vaccine rules
stories.body: Archbishop Wenski continues to resist Attorney General James Uthmeier’s pressure over religious exemptions in Catholic schools, calling it “bullying” and defending vaccination as serving the common good.

stories.headline: Europe: Assisi’s 40th-anniversary peace prayer closes today
stories.body: Christian leaders gather this afternoon in the Lower Basilica of Saint Francis, with Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew speaking and Pope Leo’s message read in his absence. The theme, “Disarmed and Disarming Peace,” is the title of the Pope’s July book.

stories.headline: Asia: Bishop Crispin Varquez installed in his hometown, Tagbilaran
stories.body: Bishop Crispin “Bai” Varquez took possession of the Diocese of Tagbilaran in Bohol, Philippines, this morning as its eighth bishop, urging “passion and enthusiasm for the work of evangelization.” Who he is: a Tagbilaran native, 65, ordained in 1989, a former seminary formator, and bishop of Borongan in Eastern Samar from 2007. He succeeds Alberto Uy, now archbishop of Cebu.

stories.headline: Africa: Kidnapped Nigerian priest freed in Benue
stories.body: Fr. John Inalegwu Otache, pastor of St. Margaret’s in Ajegbe-Awume, was rescued with seven other captives by Benue police and local vigilantes, and two suspects were arrested. The Diocese of Otukpo gave thanks “with hearts full of joy” and asked prayers for those still held, including Fr. Emmanuel Ezema of Zaria, missing since December.

stories.headline: Middle East: Jordan answers the Karak church attack with strikes in Syria
stories.body: After Friday’s attack on a funeral at St. George Orthodox Church in Hamoud, Jordan struck Islamic State targets in southern Syria and says it killed more than 20 fighters. Syria reports eight civilian deaths. Pope Leo prayed for the victims at Sunday’s Angelus.

stories.headline: North America: New York’s $800 million abuse settlement nears signing
stories.body: The Archdiocese of New York and about 1,300 survivors agreed to an 800-million-dollar settlement, to be signed the week of Nov. 6. Archbishop Ronald Hicks prayed it would “bring some measure of healing and reconciliation.”

stories.headline: Latin America: Peru, Argentina and Uruguay prepare for the Pope
stories.body: With the Pope’s medical all-clear, preparations go ahead for Nov. 6–17, from Montevideo and Luján to Chiclayo, where he was bishop, and Cuzco.

stories.headline: Appointments this week: Madagascar, Joliet, Italy and Greece
stories.body: Archbishop Jean Nicolas Rakotojaona now leads Fianarantsoa, Madagascar. He was born in 1973, holds a theology doctorate from Fribourg and was coadjutor until Sunday. Bishop Brendan Cahill, until now bishop of Victoria, Texas, will be installed in Joliet on Nov. 11. Thursday, Giorgio Ferretti takes possession of Lucera-Troia in Italy. Saturday, Georgios Altouvas is installed at Syros in Greece, and Michele Di Tolve, a Milan priest, at Chioggia.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Medjugorje Oct. 25; Countdown Oct. 25; campus revival tonight.

stories.headline: Medjugorje, Oct. 25: “Pray more strongly and more for the peace”
stories.body: The latest monthly message, given Oct. 25, 2026, through the visionary Marija: “Dear children! A fire of hatred and wars is spreading in the hearts of people who do not want peace but their own weak interests. That is why, little children, you be prayer and my extended hands of love and peace for all those who are far from my motherly heart. Pray more strongly and more for the peace that God desires to give you but you do not want it. I am with you and I am praying that peace may prevail and reign in every heart.” The next monthly message is due Nov. 25.

stories.headline: Countdown to the Kingdom: latest post Oct. 25
stories.body: Checked this morning, the newest post is still Sunday, Oct. 25: “Marija – A Fire of Hatred is Spreading,” summed up as “Pray for people who do not want peace.” Before it came “The Suicide of the West” and “Defending Your Family” on Oct. 23, and two messages attributed to Pedro Regis: “The One Who Opposes Christ” on Oct. 21 and “There Will be a Great War” on Oct. 20. The site asks readers to test every message with the Church, which alone judges authenticity.

stories.headline: The message and the night’s news, read together
stories.body: In the 48 hours since Our Lady spoke of a “fire of hatred and wars,” 16 ballistic missiles fell on Kyiv, Houthi missiles flew at Saudi cities, Jordan struck Syria over a church massacre, and El Fasher marked a year under the RSF. Against that, religious leaders from 53 nations pray in Assisi today, and a small truce lets aid reach Oleshky. The message asks for two things: be prayer, and be “extended hands of love and peace.” Jesus’ words in Matthew 24 still apply: “See that you are not alarmed.”

stories.headline: Revival on campus: UniteUS reaches South Alabama tonight
stories.body: UniteUS, the student outreach that began at Auburn in 2023, holds its next campus night tonight at the University of South Alabama. At Appalachian State this month it reported more than 700 decisions for Christ and about 100 baptisms. The ministry says it has reached more than two dozen campuses, the University of Miami among them, and more than 100,000 students. Belmont in Nashville is next, on Nov. 10.

stories.headline: Revival by the water: beach and campus baptisms keep spreading
stories.body: More than 550 people were baptized at Bridlington South Beach in England on Oct. 10, after earlier beach baptisms at Bigbury. Thousands joined the oceanfront baptisms at Oceanside, California, on Oct. 17. Local churches report students baptized after campus nights from Mississippi to Georgia. Many of these gatherings are led by local congregations, not one big organization.

stories.headline: Eucharistic: Guatemala’s Cuilapa Host under study
stories.body: Witnesses in Cuilapa, Guatemala, describe a consecrated Host that stayed intact in water for eight days and developed reddish stains. A multidisciplinary team is studying it, and the diocese stresses that only the Holy See can authorize veneration. Similar cases, such as Sokółka in Poland, took years of scientific and Church review.

stories.headline: Digital ID, soberly: Britain dropped the scheme but kept the plumbing
stories.body: Britain has scrapped its national digital ID card, the compulsory-then-voluntary plan that Prime Minister Andy Burnham ended. But officials told MPs that One Login and the government digital wallet continue, with more than 80 credential types planned and digital driving licences targeted for 2027. One MP warned of digital ID “by the back door.” In Europe, the digital euro is still being negotiated, with a pilot planned for late 2027 and possible issuance in 2029. It is real infrastructure that deserves scrutiny, not panic.

stories.body: Wednesday at 6 p.m. Miami-Dade Schools Police holds a free trunk-or-treat at 3300 NW 27th Ave. Thursday from 4 to 8, Hialeah Cares throws a free Halloween party and haunted house at Miami Dade College Hialeah. stories.headline: Thursday: VOUS Worship’s “Man Alive,” free at Bayfront Park
stories.body: VOUS Worship brings “Man Alive” to the FPL Solar Amphitheater at Bayfront Park on Thursday, Oct. 29. Doors open at 6, music runs 7 to 10, and admission is free.

stories.headline: Next week and beyond: Crowder, Miles Minnick, Gilberto Daza, Jekalyn Carr

beats.title: Pick-me-up
beats.headline: Giannis triple-double in loss; Ahsoka trailer brings back Anakin.

stories.headline: Heat: Giannis’s first Miami triple-double, but Flagg’s block sinks them
stories.body: Giannis Antetokounmpo had 29 points, 15 rebounds and 11 assists, his first triple-double with the Heat, and Davion Mitchell scored 21. But Cooper Flagg had 29 points and 11 assists, and with 31 seconds left he blocked Andrew Wiggins’s three that would have put Miami ahead. Dallas won 113–109. At 0–4, the Heat are off to their worst start since 2008–09. Next: at Atlanta Wednesday at 7, then Indiana at home Friday at 8.
stories.why: In 2008–09, the Heat started 0–4 and still made the playoffs.

stories.headline: Star Wars: Ahsoka Season 2 trailer brings back Hayden Christensen’s Anakin
stories.body: The new trailer, shown at D23, sets Ahsoka Season 2 for Jan. 20, 2027 on Disney+. Anakin returns as a Force ghost and in Clone Wars flashbacks, asking Ahsoka: “Are you a Jedi... or not?” Sabine trains with Ahsoka on Peridea, Ezra fights Death Troopers, and Rory McCann takes over as Baylan Skoll. Dave Filoni says the Mortis gods are “definitely a thing.”

stories.headline: Star Wars: Vader’s Monday Night Football interviews begin
stories.body: An animated Darth Vader began interviewing NFL players on Monday Night Football, building to an all-animated Star Wars telecast of the Super Bowl on Feb. 14, 2027. Next Tuesday, Nov. 3, the 256-page art book for The Mandalorian and Grogu arrives.
